claims: The Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
The Artemis II crew of four astronauts is currently in Earth's orbit.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day journey around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission marks the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years.
The Artemis II launch time was 6:35 p.m. EDT (22:35 UTC) on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
The rocket for the Artemis II mission was the Space Launch System (SLS).
The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II mission goal is a ~10-day trip around the Moon and back to test systems for future landings.
The Artemis II crew is safe in orbit.
The Artemis II mission is underway.
The Artemis II crew is now preparing for the next phase of the mission.
The next phase of the Artemis II mission involves departing Earth's orbit for the moon.
